target_customer: Consumers who host parties, festival campers and outdoor groups buying a loud, rugged battery speaker
problem: Portable speakers were too quiet and fragile for festivals and outdoor parties.
business_model: Direct to consumer and retail hardware sales of speakers, batteries and accessories

founders.name: Jesper Theil Thomsen
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Oct 2023) quotes him on festival origins.

founders.name: Christoffer Nyvold
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and Nordic9.

founders.name: Hjalte Emilio Wieth
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by Nordic9 (Sept 2020); not named on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Acoustic and battery design for very high volume and durability with contract manufacturing, standard consumer hardware engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Loudness and ruggedness were product features other audio firms could match; the main differentiator was brand and festival credibility.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large audio brands sold portable speakers but none bought or copied the party speaker niche in a way found in sources; Soundboks stayed independent and grew.

market_need_then: Soundboks launched on Kickstarter in March 2016 and TechCrunch reports it took $600,000 in preorders within 20 days, evidence of demand for a loud portable speaker.

identity.visual_style: Rugged, durable look; Made for mistreatment theme on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Party and festival oriented, loud and playful

branding.brand_signature: World's loudest portable speaker claim and the Made for mistreatment theme
branding.community_and_virality: Origin in a DIY speaker for Roskilde Festival, strong festival community and press coverage from Gizmodo, Maxim and Rolling Stone; described by one source as a lifeline for communal connection during the pandemic.

brand_strength.rationale: Authentic festival story, repeated press about its loudness and a recognizable product; investors cited the authentic brand and community. Name origin and merch not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Soundboks grew from a festival speaker idea and a record Danish Kickstarter into a profitable-leaning hardware brand with offices in Copenhagen and Los Angeles, backed by Heartcore and Jägermeister. Its authentic festival brand and loud product differentiated it, and modest outside capital suggests capital efficient growth.
notes: Funding totals conflict: Nordic9 says $20.07M total and TechCrunch $20.93M after the 2023 round, CB Insights $22.83M over 8 rounds, others $8.35M to $52M. The 2017 $3M and 2019 $2.3M debt figures come only from the Nordic9 article. The 2020 DKK 52M round: Nordic9 headline says to raise; TechCrunch calls Heartcore and Best Nights VC the Series A investors, but the source stage label is unclear so stage is other. TechCrunch says Soundboks launched in 2014 while YC and Nordic9 say 2015. Competitors: no dated source naming rivals around March 2016 was found, so the list is empty. Outcome search found nothing on layoffs or acquisition.
